resources.string: Every day a new pet comes as an egg, never one you have. Common ones come most often, legendary ones rarely, mythic ones almost never. Tap an egg to put it on the matrix, tap a pet to see its three forms.
Every pet you do not have yet, as an egg right away
Support n7 and get every pet now
One-time purchase. Everything else in the game is free.
Activate Glyph Pet in Glyph Toys
Hold the Glyph button to feed, and a full pet plays a mini-game. Shake it to see its signature, or to grow a pet that is ready
Set it as the Always-on Glyph Toy to keep it with you
Every day you play, a new pet comes as an egg, always one you do not have yet. Put it on the matrix and hold the Glyph button five times: it hatches.

The pet lives on the back of your phone, or in the app. Hold the Glyph button to feed it; a full one starts a mini-game you steer by tilting. Tap the back twice to stroke it. A shake shows its signature, or grows it once it is ready.

Every new pet joins your nursery: common, rare, legendary, mythic, and anomalies that come when you meet their condition. Now and then, one hatch in twenty, a shiny one comes out, shimmering like a foil card. Its album shows which of its animations you have seen.

Blow on the matrix and the wind carries your pet, each kind its own way. Clap and it starts. Lay the phone matrix up by your keyboard and type: it turns into its own little toy, each key does something, and at 10 and 20 seconds comes a finale. All of it brings it joy. When the phone rings or a notification comes, it answers first. The microphone only hears how loud it is, nothing is recorded; you turn it on in Settings.
Without it the pet will not show up on the back of your phone. Add Glyph Pet to your Glyph Toys.

Drop by for a couple of minutes when you have time. One meal is a dot of food. Every 10 seconds of a game is a dot of joy; the game costs a dot of energy. Worn out, it naps for about forty seconds; turn the phone over or charge it and it rests fast. It grows while it is on the screen, awake and fed: a teen in 15 minutes, an adult an hour later.
